description: Raw bitFlyer public execution history per product (executions_<product>.csv, deduped by execution id, the source candles_fx_btc_jpy.json's candles are resampled from), the same history pre-bucketed into 1-minute OHLCV+buy/sell-split bars (flow_<product>.csv), and the FX_BTC_JPY-vs-BTC_JPY basis computed from the 1-minute candles (basis_1m.csv). schema/candles_fx_btc_jpy.json already documents these two file shapes informally as 'companion_files'; this schema is what actually resolves their path_glob so they are checked instead of landing in schema_undefined.
source: executions_<product>.csv: bitFlyer public GET /v1/executions, paged, deduped by id (see scripts/fetch_history.py). flow_<product>.csv: the same executions resampled to 1-minute OHLCV with a buy/sell volume split. basis_1m.csv: scripts/build_basis.py, inner-joins data/candles_FX_BTC_JPY.csv and data/candles_BTC_JPY.csv on their UTC minute index and computes the FX-over-spot percentage basis.
retention: bitFlyer's public execution history is 31 days; executions_<product>.csv, flow_<product>.csv and basis_1m.csv are all long-term substitutes, appended/rebuilt forward and never regenerated in a way that drops old rows. backtest_data/executions_FX_BTC_JPY_31d_<date>.csv.gz and flow_FX_BTC_JPY_<date>.csv are permanent dated snapshots of the FX_BTC_JPY files for reproducibility.

id.meaning: bitFlyer execution id, monotonically increasing, used for incremental paging/dedup

exec_date.unit: ISO-8601 (bitFlyer's native format, mixed precision -- read with pandas format='mixed')
exec_date.notes: trade time (約定時刻), same sense as executions_*.csv.gz's ts in schema/bitflyer_tape.json

open.meaning: first execution price in the minute
open.notes: forward-filled from the previous real minute when synthetic=1

high.meaning: max execution price in the minute
high.notes: forward-filled from the previous real minute when synthetic=1

low.meaning: min execution price in the minute
low.notes: forward-filled from the previous real minute when synthetic=1

close.meaning: last execution price in the minute
close.notes: forward-filled from the previous real minute when synthetic=1

volume.meaning: total execution size in the minute (buy_vol + sell_vol)

synthetic.meaning: 1 = this minute had zero executions and every OHLCV column above is forward-filled/zeroed rather than observed; 0 = a real minute
synthetic.notes: added 2026-09-05 (DATA QA); rows written before this date do not have this column at all -- its absence, not a 0 value, is what marks pre-fix history

ts.meaning: 1-minute UTC index shared by candles_FX_BTC_JPY.csv and candles_BTC_JPY.csv (inner join -- a minute either book was quiet in produces no row)

basis_pct.notes: positive = FX trading above spot (contango); negative = below (backwardation)

known_defects: executions_<product>.csv duplicate_keys should be checked on id, not exec_date -- several executions can share the same exec_date microsecond (see schema/bitflyer_tape.json's executions_YYYYMMDD.csv.gz for the same phenomenon on the WS-derived tape)
basis_1m.csv silently omits a minute with zero executions (no interpolated/zero row) -- a gap in ts is a genuinely quiet minute for that product/pair, not necessarily a collection failure

basis_1m.csv is rebuilt from data/candles_FX_BTC_JPY.csv and data/candles_BTC_JPY.csv on every run of scripts/build_basis.py -- a correction to either candle file would silently change historical basis_pct values

DATA QA 2026-09-05 (docs/DATA_QA_TRIAGE.md): flow_<product>.csv's maintenance_window (80) and zero_volume (2527) flags root-caused to scripts/build_flow.py independently reimplementing scripts/fetch_deep.py's ffill(open/high/low/close)+fillna(0.0) gap-filling -- UNLIKE the note above (which describes fetch_history.py's build_candles, which drops quiet minutes entirely), build_flow.py never dropped them, it just had no way to mark them. Fixed by adding the same `synthetic` flag fetch_deep.py already has (see the column doc above and tests/test_build_flow.py); existing data/flow_*.csv files are not rewritten.

DATA QA 2026-09-05: executions_<product>.csv's non_monotonic (538,325 rows, on data/executions_FX_BTC_JPY.csv and data/executions_XRP_JPY.csv only -- NOT on the backtest_data/executions_FX_BTC_JPY_31d_*.csv.gz snapshot, which is built by a separate, already-sorted extraction path) and a large share of its gaps (109,005 total across the dataset) are the same root cause: scripts/fetch_history.py pages backward from the newest trade each run (before=None, then before=<oldest id so far>) and used to append that batch to the file in the newest-first order it arrived in, writing a strictly-decreasing id/timestamp run into an otherwise-ascending file on every single run -- and a gaps check computed off that same broken row order manufactures bogus deltas alongside the real non_monotonic ones. Fixed: scripts/fetch_history.py now sorts each run's new rows ascending by id before appending (see `_order_new_rows`, tests/test_fetch_history_candles.py). Existing rows are NOT reordered -- the historical reversed runs already written remain and will keep flagging non_monotonic/gaps until/unless a one-off resort of the existing file is separately decided (not done here: never modify data files).

DATA QA 2026-09-05: checked group_by applicability for flow_<product>.csv and executions_<product>.csv -- confirmed NOT interleaved (one file per product already, verified against backtest_data/flow_FX_BTC_JPY_20260820.csv and backtest_data/executions_FX_BTC_JPY_31d_*.csv.gz headers), so quality.group_by is not needed here; the gaps/non_monotonic counts are fully explained by the ordering bug above, not by multiple symbols sharing one file.
